quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you meet all these conditions:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You need all three conditions to pass safely: you must see the road ahead clearly, you must be able to get back to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your car must be fast enough to pass. Only pass when it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right.
The vehicle approaching from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control signs or signals, you must yield to the vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Which of these statements about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use loudspeakers to give instructions.
They may follow each other closely.

questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so wait until you are sure the way is clear before moving.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Look for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you, use your turn signal to alert other drivers, and look for other drivers in the same lane. Do not use your phone while driving.

questions.question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You may only go in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only go in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a hospital with emergency services is ahead and to the right.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. Any activity that takes your attention away from driving is dangerous. Keep your full focus on the road.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, a driver must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn, and go when the intersection is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, release the gas pedal. Do not brake. Keep the steering wheel straight. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.question: Who can use HOV lanes?

options.text: Vehicles with more than one person in them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles with more than one person in them.
questions.explanation: HOV stands for High Occupancy Vehicles. HOV lanes are for vehicles with more than one person. Signs show how many people must be in the vehicle. Signs also show what days and hours the rule applies.

questions.question: What are signs that show dangerous road conditions called?
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazardous conditions. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident and show careless driving.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into your original lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to your original lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough room to pull in safely in front of that vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children leave the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm is out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled in before moving. After the bus moves, wait until you are sure no children are crossing the road before you drive.

questions.question: Where are U-turns not allowed?

options.text: On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road with clear visibility for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or pedestrians. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when a traffic light turns green?

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let any pedestrians and vehicles that are still in the intersection cross safely.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones?
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 15 miles per hour. Drive extra carefully in areas where children or other pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When are crashes most likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at the same speed.
When one lane travels faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes are more likely when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases your risk of a crash. Driving slower than traffic is also dangerous. It can cause rear-end crashes or force other drivers to swerve around you.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or road narrows ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or road narrows ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign tells you that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: This sign shows:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign warns you that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other roadside objects.
